expected_behaviour: A result file over 50 MB from one PC, or 200 MB per artifact across PCs, is held rather than imported; the rest of the hunt imports.

feature: Held results Import anyway or Skip
user_story: As an analyst I decide what to do with an oversized held result.
expected_behaviour: Held results (zips, unzipped hunts, single files, bundle hunts) wait in drop/_held/; Import anyway moves the file back into drop/ and imports it, Skip moves it to drop/_skipped/.

user_story: As an analyst I have a collected bundle hunt hold oversized artifacts.
expected_behaviour: A collected bundle hunt holds an artifact over 50 MB from one PC or 200 MB across PCs for Import anyway or Skip, like a dropped hunt zip.

user_story: As an analyst I see how far a dropped hunt zip has got.
expected_behaviour: The Jobs row counts result files done of total, names the file importing, and shows an ETA.

user_story: As an analyst I import a very large Velociraptor export without the server running out of memory.
expected_behaviour: Rows are settled in pages so memory stays bounded and the dashboard stays responsive during a large import.

feature: Velociraptor re-import reads only what changed
user_story: As an analyst I re-import a hunt or flow and read only what is new.
expected_behaviour: Import re-reads only artifacts that were cut short, failed or grew since the last import; a hunt already in the case imports nothing until Re-import anyway is chosen.

user_story: As an analyst I import a large notebook export in JSON Lines form.
expected_behaviour: A notebook export is detected as Velociraptor and large files stream from disk.

user_story: As an analyst I am protected from a VQL query hiding control characters.
expected_behaviour: Control, zero-width and text-direction characters in any launched VQL are refused with a clear error.

user_story: As an operator I raise the cap on collected output.
expected_behaviour: DFIR_VELOCIRAPTOR_COLLECT_MAX_OUTPUT defaults to 400 MB and bounds one collection's output.

user_story: As an analyst I run bundles, import GUI hunts and monitor live from one case panel.
expected_behaviour: The Fleet Collection panel holds bundle runs, GUI hunt or flow import and live monitoring for the open case.

user_story: As an analyst I do not lose the server to a file that crashes the import.
expected_behaviour: A streamed drop file that crashed the server twice at the same version is refused and moved to _failed/ with a reason.

feature: Drop log and status written per file
user_story: As an analyst I keep the drop log intact if the sweep stops mid-way.
expected_behaviour: Each dropped file's log line and status entry are written as it finishes.

user_story: As an analyst I get a clear refusal instead of a crash on a huge case.
expected_behaviour: An import that would exhaust memory is refused with a message naming the case size and a suggested way forward.

feature: Import progress bar with rate and ETA
user_story: As an analyst I see import progress.
expected_behaviour: Every job row with progress draws a bar with rate and ETA; an external hunt or flow import is a cancellable job.

feature: Custody at receipt with SHA-256 and SHA-1
user_story: As an analyst I have every import hashed on arrival.
expected_behaviour: Every import is hashed with SHA-256 and SHA-1 into chain of custody before any parser runs, including rejected files.

user_story: As an analyst I import a case ZIP made by Archive to ZIP.
expected_behaviour: Import case accepts the ZIP and checks paths, case identity and manifest hashes before it writes anything.

user_story: As an analyst I import Falcon exports.
expected_behaviour: Event Search, LogScale, FDR, Next-Gen SIEM and alert exports import with host, user, IP, domain and hash IOCs and logons; alerts keep Falcon's severity.

feature: NG-SIEM connection Test and Run in Falcon
user_story: As an analyst I test the CrowdStrike Next-Gen SIEM connection and run CQL hunts.
expected_behaviour: Test runs a step-by-step sign-in, write and read check with named failure reasons, capped at 5 per minute; Run in Falcon imports rows as evidence; Open in Falcon links only to real console hosts.

feature: Main evidence source and hunt language
user_story: As an analyst I set my main evidence tool so hunts use its query language.
expected_behaviour: The main evidence source (CQL, KQL, ES|QL, SPL or VQL) is set at case creation or in Settings and drives hunts, next steps and synthesis wording; Carbon Black, Wazuh, SentinelOne, Cortex XDR and QRadar get hunts in their own language.

user_story: As an analyst I keep each case's IRIS, Timesketch and Velociraptor servers separate.
expected_behaviour: Each case remembers its own server set; Settings and Reconnect follow the open case's set.

user_story: As an operator I use a cheaper model for query hunts and translation.
expected_behaviour: An optional light-task model handles CQL, KQL, ES|QL and SPL hunts and query translation; Diagnostics names each task's model.

user_story: As an administrator I forward each case's activity log to a SIEM.
expected_behaviour: Per destination opt-in forwards the log to Splunk HEC, Elasticsearch or syslog and replays safely after a failure.

user_story: As an analyst I see other cases sharing an indicator.
expected_behaviour: When DFIR_CROSS_CASE=on the Related Cases panel lists cases sharing an indicator; otherwise it stays off.

user_story: As an analyst I open a case as a threat hunt so the AI frames findings as hunt results.
expected_behaviour: A threat-hunt case gets hunt framing in the AI prompts and a hunt summary report; Convert to incident turns it into an ordinary incident case.

user_story: As an analyst I see how many hosts show an item so rare items stand out.
expected_behaviour: Hunt items show 'seen on N of M hosts' and are graded by prevalence; startup items and tasks are keyed by the program they run.

user_story: As an administrator I record what a client normally runs so it is not flagged again.
expected_behaviour: Admin-only client baselines hold approvals matched by path, Amcache SHA1 or verified signer; approvals go through a confirm list; items with no path say why they cannot be approved.

user_story: As an administrator I choose which categories a baseline download covers.
expected_behaviour: The Client Baseline panel has a Download policy block with category tick boxes and standard buttons and inputs.

user_story: As an analyst I re-grade a hunt after the baseline changes.
expected_behaviour: Re-grade applies the current baseline to existing hunt items and updates grades, including 'new since last hunt'.

user_story: As an analyst I get a hunt summary in the report.
expected_behaviour: A threat-hunt case's report includes a hunt summary of items, prevalence and baseline decisions.

user_story: As the instance administrator I create a client from the New Case dialog.
expected_behaviour: The Client box in New Case offers creating a new client in place; non-administrators do not see it.

user_story: As an analyst I collect cloud logs straight from AWS, Microsoft 365 and GCP into a case.
expected_behaviour: CloudTrail (S3 trails or 90-day history), M365 audit log, Entra, Azure Activity and GCP audit logs are collected as hashed, manifest-backed evidence and imported.

user_story: As an analyst I resume a cloud collection that stopped.
expected_behaviour: Cloud collection jobs survive restarts; every page is SHA-256'd into an append-only manifest; results are complete, partial or failed and a stopped job resumes without repeating members.

user_story: As an analyst I see the cost of a collection before it runs.
expected_behaviour: A pre-check estimates volume, capped windows split automatically, a per-tenant Microsoft query budget applies and cutoffs are disclosed.

feature: AWS region picker and GuardDuty findings
user_story: As an analyst I choose AWS regions and collect GuardDuty findings.
expected_behaviour: Collection walks the account's enabled regions with untick and skipped regions disclosed; GuardDuty findings are collected from every detector region and graded by severity with MITRE from the finding type.

user_story: As an administrator I store cloud accounts safely.
expected_behaviour: AWS accounts, Microsoft tenants and GCP projects are kept in their own Settings tab with secrets sealed by a separate key file; a failed write leaves no temp copy.

user_story: As a case writer I only see cloud accounts attached to my cases.
expected_behaviour: In team mode only writers of the attached cases see or use an account; the public demo refuses cloud routes.

user_story: As an analyst I test an account before collecting.
expected_behaviour: Check access tests one read per source and shows minimum AWS, Microsoft and GCP policies; GCP and Microsoft checks show no AWS-only fields.

feature: Cloud credentials end with the case
user_story: As an administrator I stop credentials outliving the case.
expected_behaviour: Closing a case offers Delete or Keep for its cloud credentials; archive and delete always remove them; a held-credential list shows audit and custody.

user_story: As an operator I route cloud SDK traffic through my proxy and CA.
expected_behaviour: DFIR_CLOUD_CA, DFIR_CLOUD_INSECURE and DFIR_CLOUD_PROXY_URL are applied to all cloud SDK traffic.

feature: Cloud Coverage and AWS account weaknesses
user_story: As an analyst I see what cloud logging covers and what is weak.
expected_behaviour: Cloud Coverage lists sources with one row per account; AWS weaknesses (root without MFA, routine root use, no Object Lock, S3 data-event gaps) show in a CSV and report section.

feature: Cloud trusted sources and identity labels
user_story: As an analyst I label cloud IPs, keys and principals as ours, responder or attacker.
expected_behaviour: Trusted sources get a hideable trusted-activity label with grades unchanged; cloud identities become IOCs with labels attacker, ours, responder or unknown; collector calls are tagged and can be hidden.

feature: Cloud export recognition and record dedup
user_story: As an analyst I import any common cloud export without duplicates.
expected_behaviour: Log Analytics, MES mailbox audit, CloudTrail console CSV, Graph audit and Azure diagnostic exports reach the right importer; overlapping exports add no duplicate rows and conflicts are flagged.

feature: Sigma rule updates, exclusions and re-grade
user_story: As an analyst I keep Sigma rules current and re-grade a case with them.
expected_behaviour: Check, preview, install and roll back SigmaHQ and Suzaku releases; add exclusions with a reason; preview then apply a re-grade of imported cloud and web-log events, with measuring a release against the case first.

feature: Sigma coverage card and dry run
user_story: As an analyst I check whether Sigma rules cover my log sources and test a pasted rule.
expected_behaviour: The Hunt Workbench coverage card shows per log source whether Sigma graded it; the paste card counts matching events and names fields the case cannot check.

user_story: As an administrator I update tagger rules without an app release.
expected_behaviour: Curated tagger rules publish as rules-* releases that can be checked, installed, measured and rolled back; edited tagger copies take new built-in rules while keeping edits.

user_story: As an analyst I check chosen endpoints for tampered AI coding agents.
expected_behaviour: Launching picks endpoints and runs the ai-dfir-toolkit YARA and Sigma rules through Velociraptor, listing poisoned instruction files, rogue MCP servers and hooks with provisional grades; case writers see their case's endpoints and no-case runs are admin-only.

feature: AI Agent Forensics evidence and Add to case
user_story: As an analyst I read the evidence for each match and file it into a case.
expected_behaviour: Each match shows file hash, preserved-copy hash and per-rule Sigma coverage; matched text stays away from the AI; Add to case keys events by client id and keeps a report-safe copy that Re-read refreshes.

user_story: As an analyst I see every AI-agent run in the case report.
expected_behaviour: The report lists each run launched in or filed into the case with inventory, matched text, both hashes, Sigma coverage and rules not run.

feature: Missed evidence review by decision model
user_story: As an analyst I have a fast model grade the Info rows the tagger left behind.
expected_behaviour: The analyst-pressed review grades Info rows, shows a confidence filter starting at 40% and a cap warning, and ticked rows are promoted into the forensic timeline.

user_story: As an administrator I pick which OpenRouter model runs the missed-evidence review and containment check.
expected_behaviour: Settings lists OpenRouter models for the decision model, shows its key source, and the review and containment check use it.

user_story: As an analyst I check whether a finding's cited evidence supports containment steps.
expected_behaviour: The check answers narrow questions about the cited evidence and a tested rule suggests containment steps for the finding.

user_story: As an analyst I let a referee model judge each disagreement.
expected_behaviour: Models are labelled A and B; a configurable referee judges each disagreement from the cited events; Follow the referee accepts or rejects all pending deltas in one click and lists deltas it made no call on.

user_story: As an analyst I see when the main model changes a finding I already decided.
expected_behaviour: A finding with a new main-model call is marked reopened and keeps the analyst's earlier decision visible.

user_story: As an analyst I still get a synthesis when the model's safety filter stops it.
expected_behaviour: A stopped synthesis is retried and then falls back once to the fallback model chosen in Settings; the note names the model used; the default referee, Explain event and view summaries do the same.

user_story: As an operator I save a safety-stopped prompt for replay.
expected_behaviour: With DFIR_AI_CAPTURE_SAFETY_STOPS on, a safety-stopped prompt is saved into the case folder.

feature: Preview what the AI will see
user_story: As an analyst I see the first request an AI action would send before it goes.
expected_behaviour: The Anon dialog shows clear and masked text side by side as a diff, with a summary by kind and a show-only-changed switch; nothing is sent.

feature: AI switch blocks every AI call
user_story: As an analyst I switch AI off for a case and know nothing is sent to a model.
expected_behaviour: While the case's AI is off no AI call is made by any route, import, Watson or background job; deterministic importing and grading still run.

fix: Fixed in PR #2780

user_story: As an analyst I can only archive a case after closing it.
expected_behaviour: Archiving an open case is refused with a message to close it first; an archived case refuses status changes until restored.
test_result: QA round 1: an open case could be archived; fixed in #2780
fix: Fixed in PR #2780

user_story: As an analyst I trust a closed case does not change.
expected_behaviour: Every change outside a reviewed allowlist, including imports and ingest, is refused for a closed or archived case; closing cancels running AI work; another analyst's close refreshes open dashboards.

user_story: As a team user I stay signed in while active.
expected_behaviour: Activity extends a session up to a hard limit (DFIR_AUTH_SESSION_MAX_HOURS, default 7 days); idle sessions still expire.

user_story: As a case owner I mint one capture token for every case I can edit.
expected_behaviour: The token is capped at capture plus write, lasts at most 90 days and only reaches cases its owner can edit.

feature: Live dashboards closed on access change
user_story: As an administrator I cut off a user's live dashboard when access changes.
expected_behaviour: Password change, sign-out, disable, demotion or role removal closes that user's live dashboard connections.

user_story: As an operator I get HTTPS without setting up certificates.
expected_behaviour: HTTPS is on by default in team mode with a private local CA and silent renewal; behind a plain-HTTP proxy DFIR_HTTPS=off; the extension names an untrusted certificate.

user_story: As an operator I am protected from web pages and DNS rebinding reaching the local API.
expected_behaviour: An unrecognised Host name or a foreign browser Origin gets 403 before the route runs; no-Origin callers like curl and scripts still work; names are added with DFIR_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.

user_story: As an operator I run a public demo that cannot be abused.
expected_behaviour: With DFIR_DEMO_MODE the API blocks mutating routes except seeding, seeds the demo case at startup and resets it hourly; remote binding needs DFIR_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_REMOTE=public-demo.

user_story: As an operator I see when the server is listening.
expected_behaviour: An ASCII banner with the dashboard URL prints when the server is ready.

user_story: As an analyst I download one redacted zip for a bug report.
expected_behaviour: Diagnostics previews and downloads a zip of redacted logs, a capped debug log and failed-import layouts; usernames and Watson-masked names are redacted.

user_story: As an administrator I remove a saved secret.
expected_behaviour: Secret settings have a Clear button; an emptied field removes its key; on/off settings are drop-downs.

feature: Per-provider AI keys and base URLs
user_story: As an administrator I save one key and base URL per AI provider.
expected_behaviour: Any model can switch providers without retyping keys; per-model fields are overrides in the full Settings view.

user_story: As an analyst I set the dashboard text size, body font and code font.
expected_behaviour: The chosen size and fonts apply across the dashboard and persist.

user_story: As an analyst I hand a case over at shift change with a brief.
expected_behaviour: The Handoff Brief lists findings by owner, open questions, hypotheses, next steps, unchecked IOCs and the outgoing analyst's note; copy as Markdown; opt-in report section.

feature: Story so far and Now next steps
user_story: As an analyst I read the case as a story in the Now cockpit.
expected_behaviour: One card per kill-chain stage shows intrusion shape and greyed missing stages with copy-as-brief; the top three playbook steps show after Open hypotheses.

user_story: As an analyst I see Kerberoasting per service account.
expected_behaviour: Per service account the panel shows 4769 requests, baseline, later use by the exact account and first-seen-host use; also a report section.

user_story: As an analyst I see who a phishing campaign reached.
expected_behaviour: Per message the panel shows who was addressed, what was delivered and attachments, and per host what its own rows establish about execution and control.

user_story: As an analyst I review findings whose threat intel is no longer actionable.
expected_behaviour: The panel lists findings whose intel assertions expired or were revoked, with a per-finding decision; expired assertions stay recorded.

user_story: As an analyst I see and override the evidence collection plan.
expected_behaviour: The panel lists collection steps with generation diffs and lets the analyst override or restore a step to automatic.

feature: Hunt Workbench saved hunts and history
user_story: As an analyst I save a hunt and see its runs.
expected_behaviour: A saved hunt lists runs newest first with time, analyst, status, matches and duration; the reference and field catalogue load when the case opens.

user_story: As an analyst I check for recurrence after remediation.
expected_behaviour: After a remediation boundary is declared, Verify returns facts only with coverage stated; the panel and report section list them.

user_story: As an analyst I read what a web root exposed.
expected_behaviour: With a web root declared, each file shows suspected exposure, retrieval requested, response size and corroborated disclosure.

user_story: As an analyst I read access to files that matter.
expected_behaviour: Declared files are read per object from 4663, 4656, 5145 and 4660 with process and logon session as candidates.

user_story: As an analyst I see TLS relationships across the case.
expected_behaviour: Zeek and Suricata TLS records become a case-wide graph with JA3S nodes and certificate chains.

user_story: As an analyst I read coverage on a Navigator-style matrix.
expected_behaviour: The MITRE panel and interactive report show an offline matrix with platform filter, hits-only view and per-technique counts.

user_story: As an analyst I fold identical super-timeline runs.
expected_behaviour: Group repeats folds identical runs into one xN row; nothing is merged.

user_story: As an analyst I record what an attack achieved.
expected_behaviour: Each finding records execution (observed or not) and control (blocked, remediated, failed, allowed, none) separately, set by the analyst and kept across synthesis.

user_story: As an analyst I lift a grading cap on one finding.
expected_behaviour: A finding lowered by a grading check shows the cap and a Restore button that lifts it and is logged.

user_story: As an analyst I am warned before exporting live indicators.
expected_behaviour: Every human-readable export is checked for live indicators and unescaped evidence; a hit ships with a banner and a status warning.

user_story: As an analyst I see look-alike account and host flags.
expected_behaviour: A new account or group member one edit from a case account or built-in name is graded High.

feature: Case picker shows names and ids
user_story: As an analyst I tell same-name cases apart.
expected_behaviour: The case list shows name and case ID, same-name cases as name (id); hover shows full name and id and the open case is marked Current.

user_story: As an analyst I open a map of every input to output.
expected_behaviour: A self-contained docs page traces inputs through grading to outputs, opened from a dashboard panel.
